item.title: Nagasaki Kunchi Festival — Guide
item.description: Nagasaki Kunchi, held every year from 7–9 October, is the grand autumn festival of Suwa Shrine and one of Japan’s most spectacular and internationally flavoured festivals, listed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Dating back nearly 400 years, it showcases the city’s unique cosmopolitan culture through dazzling performances (hono-odori) presented by the city’s neighbourhoods, which take turns each year. The most famous is the electrifying Dragon Dance (Ja Odori), of Chinese origin, in which a long serpentine dragon chases a golden ball to pounding drums, but the festival also features spectacular spinning floats — dashi and elaborate boat- and whale-shaped floats hauled and spun by teams — reflecting Dutch, Chinese and Japanese influences.
